summary.en-US: One click opens your current Firefox tab in Chrome. Right-click to open this window’s web tabs. Free Windows helper required.

description.en-US:
One click. Your tab in Chrome.

Chrome Hop opens the current HTTP or HTTPS page in your installed Google Chrome on Windows 11, keeping your Firefox tab open. Pin the button to your Firefox toolbar and click it when you want to switch browsers. Localhost web pages work too.

A separate, free Windows helper is required. On the add-on’s setup page, click Download for Windows, open the downloaded installer and follow the steps. View on GitHub is a separate button for source and release details. Direct download: https://github.com/aspendesign/chrome-hop/releases/latest/download/ChromeHop-Setup-windows-x64.exe . Run it once for your Windows account. No administrator access or runtime downloads are needed. Google Chrome Stable must be installed in its normal Windows location.

Left-click still opens only the current tab immediately. Right-click the toolbar button and choose Open all tabs in this window to open its HTTP(S) tabs in order, keeping Firefox tabs open and skipping unsupported pages.

Chrome Hop uses activeTab, nativeMessaging and menus. The bulk action asks for optional tabs permission to read the selected window’s tab addresses. It queries those addresses only when you choose that menu item. Single-tab opening does not request this permission. It has no content scripts, persistent website permissions, background tab monitoring, history/cookie API, telemetry, background service, custom executable command or shell. The standalone Go helper accepts only one validated HTTP(S) URL.

Privacy: clicking the button sends the selected address to the helper and Chrome on your computer. Mozilla classifies this local transfer as browsing activity. Chrome Hop does not store or log the address or send it to a developer server. Chrome loads the address normally using its own profile and settings; Firefox login sessions and page state are not copied.

Windows 11 x64, Firefox 142+ and Google Chrome Stable. Other operating systems, custom Chrome paths, Beta/Canary and other Chromium browsers are not supported in version 1. Independent open-source project; not affiliated with Mozilla or Google.

privacy_policy.en-US:
# Chrome Hop privacy policy

Effective October 21, 2026. Applies to the Firefox add-on and Windows helper.

**Clicking Chrome Hop sends the current tab’s HTTP(S) address to the Chrome
Hop helper on your computer, which passes it to your installed Google Chrome.**
The address can include its path, query string and fragment. Right-clicking
the toolbar button and selecting **Open all tabs in this window** sends the
HTTP(S) addresses of that window’s tabs, one by one, after you allow optional
tab-address access. Other windows are excluded. Unsupported tabs are skipped.
No web address is transferred until you invoke one of these actions.

Chrome Hop does not collect browsing history, read page content, copy cookies,
transfer passwords, monitor tabs in the background, inject scripts into websites, or store
URLs. It has no accounts, analytics, advertising, telemetry, URL logs or crash
reporting. Neither the add-on nor the helper makes network requests. The
developer receives no information through the product.

Mozilla treats the local native-message handoff as data transmission, so the
manifest accurately declares the `browsingActivity` data category. It is needed
to send the address or current-window addresses you explicitly choose to the
local helper and Chrome. Required permissions are `activeTab`, `nativeMessaging`
and `menus`. The optional `tabs` permission is requested only by **Open all tabs**;
Firefox remembers a grant until you revoke it. Left-click does not request it.
Chrome Hop does not read tab titles, page content or historical visits. A tab
snapshot exists in memory for the batch and is not logged, stored or uploaded.

Chrome itself loads the selected address and may keep history, use cookies,
sync data, or contact network services according to your Chrome settings and
Google’s policies. A site may see the same address twice, once in each browser.
Firefox login sessions and page state are not copied. Avoid sending a URL with
a sensitive token unless you want Chrome to receive it. Credentials embedded
as `user:password@host` are rejected.

The installer stores its helper, host descriptor, license, install instructions
and uninstaller under your local application directory. Its HKCU registry
entries register that helper and its uninstaller. It does not scan or modify
browser profiles. Uninstall removes the helper and its registration.

GitHub handles repository visits, downloads and voluntary issue reports under
its own policies. Mozilla handles add-on installation/update requests under its
own policies. Please remove private URLs, tokens and personal data before
posting an issue. For security reports, see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/aspendesign/chrome-hop/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

version.approval_notes:
Windows 11 x64. Version 1.1.0 preserves immediate activeTab left-click opening and adds a toolbar-only menus context: Open all tabs in this window. It calls permissions.request for optional tabs synchronously from that explicit menu gesture, queries only its windowId after approval, skips unsupported URLs and sends sequential single-URL messages to the unchanged strict native helper. No automatic scanning, host permissions, injected scripts, telemetry or network APIs. Permission denial leaves ordinary left-click working. The local URL handoff is disclosed as browsingActivity.

Raw extension files are readable and untransformed. Full source, tests, threat model and installer: https://github.com/aspendesign/chrome-hop/tree/v1.1.0 . Reproduce on Windows with Go 1.27.3, Node 24.15.0, Inno 7.1.0 and Python 3.11+: python scripts/bootstrap.py; python scripts/build.py. Install the helper from the matching GitHub release. Left-click https://example.com/; Chrome opens it and Firefox stays open. Create two safe web tabs; right-click the action and select Open all tabs in this window, then allow optional tab access. Actual Firefox/Chrome smoke tests and 39 unit tests passed on ASUS. Missing helper shows a packaged direct-download page. The helper binary is byte-identical to the previously supplied 1.0.0 helper. Every Firefox source file is in the XPI; there is no minification, compilation or external extension code to reconstruct.

release_notes.en-US: Left-click still opens the current tab immediately. Right-click the Chrome Hop toolbar button and choose Open all tabs in this window to open its web tabs in order, keeping Firefox tabs open. The bulk option asks for optional tab-address access; declining leaves single-tab use unchanged. Setup now has a direct Download for Windows button and a separate View on GitHub button, three clear steps, and correct error messages.
